fields.climate: tropical; hot, humid; more moderate in highlands
fields.terrain: mostly coastal lowlands; larger islands have interior mountains
fields.hazards: occasional floods; severe droughts; tsunamis; earthquakes; volcanoes; forest fires; volcanism: Indonesia contains the most volcanoes of any country in the world, with over 75 historically active…
fields.resources: petroleum, tin, natural gas, nickel, timber, bauxite, copper, fertile soils, coal, gold, silver
fields.farm: oil palm fruit, rice, sugarcane, maize, coconuts, cassava, bananas, eggs, chicken, mangoes/guavas
fields.exports: coal, palm oil, iron alloys, lignite, garments
fields.industries: petroleum and natural gas, textiles, automotive, electrical appliances, apparel, footwear, mining, cement, medical instruments and appliances, handicrafts, chemical fertilizers, plywood, rubber…
fields.languages: Bahasa Indonesia (official, modified form of Malay), English, Dutch, local dialects (of which the most widely spoken is Javanese); note - more than 700 languages are used in Indonesia
fields.religions: Muslim 87.4%, Protestant 7.5%, Roman Catholic 3.1%, Hindu 1.7%, other 0.8% (includes Buddhist and Confucian)
fields.regions: 35 provinces, 1 autonomous province, 1 special region, and 1 national capital district
fields.legal: civil law system based on the Roman-Dutch model and influenced by customary law
fields.suffrage: 17 years of age; universal; married persons regardless of age
fields.military: 18 years of age for voluntary service for men and women; upper age limits vary by military service, position, specialty; compulsory service authorized but not utilized
